# Estimated truncation bounds for the GB2 tree, threshold and shape families

TASK-475, source revision `33c09329`. The sample is nonempty and finite. Holds fix the named parent coefficients, and the likelihood uses the inside density at a declared closed support endpoint. Attainment means a **positive finite** maximum. An infinite density at an included endpoint is recorded separately. The analysis uses the fitted shape branch for GEV and GPD where the inherited proof requires it.

## Corrections and scope

**A tight event can be null even when the nominal interval has positive width.** For the exact sample $(1)$, hold triangular $(a,b,c)=(0,1,1)$ and fix the upper cut at 2. The tight window $[1,2]$ retains only the endpoint. But with lower cut $1-\varepsilon$ the likelihood is $2/(2\varepsilon-\varepsilon^2)$, which diverges, and the retained laws tend weakly to $\delta_1$. This is a qualification to the estimated-bound reduction if it is applied merely by checking the nominal widths. On the same held interval with mode 0, the density at 1 is zero, so these loosenings have zero likelihood. With GPD $(\mu,\sigma,\xi)=(0,1,-1)$ the first example instead has height $1/\varepsilon$. With the same GPD and sample $(0)$, the lower-estimated design with fixed upper cut 1 has height one at every lower cut at or below zero. Thus even a unique, all-held parent can have a continuum of optimal nominal cuts.

**A divergent GPD likelihood can have escaping mass on a right ray.** The known-window failure list requires the qualification already identified in the independent review. For $(1,2)$, let $\mu=1$, $s\downarrow0$, $h=s^{1/4}$, $\xi=1/h$ and $\sigma=s/h$. On the lower-estimated design with fixed upper cut $\infty$, retention is one and the likelihood is $(h/s)^2(1+1/s)^{-h-1}\sim s^{-1/2}$. The conditional survival at each positive excess tends to one. On $[1,2]$ the same path has mass asymptotic to $h\log(1+1/s)$ and the conditional CDF at each excess in $(0,1)$ tends to one, so the tight bounded laws instead converge to $\delta_1$. The same divergence witness does not identify a common limit law for the three regimes. [Known-window review](2026-11-27-mod-rev9-report.md#gpd-and-pareto-iv-joint-escapes)

The zeta domain reversal and the $[1,\infty]$ alias in the earlier review qualify transfers across windows that change the admissible parent law. None of the 25 families uses such a window-specific extension in this study. Dgamma uses its positive shape and rate domain on every retained set. [Estimated-bound proof](2026-11-27-trunc-est-math-report.md#joint-profiling-lemma) · [Review](2026-11-27-mod-rev5-report.md#proof-errors-and-scope-corrections)

## Joint profiling lemma

**Proved.** Write $m=\min_i x_i$ and $M=\max_i x_i$. Denote fixed cuts by $A,B$ and the tight nominal window by $W_*=[\ell_*,u_*]$, one of $[m,B]$, $[A,M]$ or $[m,M]$. Require $A\le m$ and $B\ge M$ wherever those cuts are fixed. For each admissible parent coefficient vector $\theta$, set $S_\theta$ to its support and $C_\theta=\prod_i f_\theta(x_i)$. For every admissible nominal containing window $W$ we have
$$
 W_*\cap S_\theta\subseteq W\cap S_\theta,\qquad
 L(\theta,W)=\frac{C_\theta}{P_\theta(W)^n}.
$$
The inclusion is at the *same* coefficient vector. In particular, if $\theta_j$ moves the support, it applies separately at every $\theta_j$. On positive finite numerator and positive tight mass,
$$
 L(\theta,W)=L(\theta,W_*)\left(\frac{P_\theta(W_*)}{P_\theta(W)}\right)^n\le L(\theta,W_*).
$$
The tight pair itself is available. These two inequalities identify the joint supremum on these slices with the supremum of the tight problem. A tight maximizer gives a joint maximizer, and every finite positive joint maximizer must have maximizing tight coefficients and must add zero parent mass. An escaping tight sequence already gives a joint sequence at the same heights with fixed tight cuts. The proof uses neither an exponential-family form nor a fixed support. A zero sample density cannot give a positive finite maximum. A singular positive sample product with positive event mass gives infinite likelihood under the inside-density convention. If an observation has zero density, the positive-carrier arguments do not apply, including when a different observation is singular. Outside-support observations are incompatible.

For a continuous parent with positive density on the interior $(d_\theta,e_\theta)$, the conditional effective ends are
$$
 L_\theta=\max(\ell_*,d_\theta),\qquad U_\theta=\min(u_*,e_\theta).
$$
At a positive finite fit the nominal lower cut must equal $m$ if $d_\theta<m$, and can be any cut $\le m$ if $d_\theta=m$. The nominal upper cut must equal $M$ if $e_\theta>M$, and can be any cut $\ge M$ if $e_\theta=M$. Apply each condition only to an estimated side. Compatibility rules out $d_\theta>m$ or $e_\theta<M$. The strict statements follow by integrating strictly positive density on the open interval between the changed effective endpoints. With both cuts estimated the allowed lower and upper intervals form a Cartesian product for each winning $\theta$. Coincidence with a fitted support endpoint gives a plateau even when the parent coefficients themselves are unique.

**Proved, null tight slices.** For an atomless parent with interval support in this study, a compatible null tight slice can occur only at a constant sample $c$. For every such coefficient vector test whether a looser allowed window retains a nonempty support interval and whether $0<f_\theta(c)<\infty$. If so, take the loosened window back toward $W_*$ while keeping that vector fixed. The positive mass decreases to zero and the likelihood diverges. The effective interval shrinks to $c$, so the conditional law tends weakly to $\delta_c$. For the finite positive endpoint densities here the conditional height per observation is asymptotic to inverse effective width, by the inside limit for the density. If a looser window has positive mass and the occupied endpoint is singular, the extended likelihood is already infinite. Shrinking that window also gives a weak point mass, with infinite heights throughout that fixed-coefficient trace. If no loosened window has positive mass, the null slice is infeasible. If loosenings have positive mass but density zero at $c$, they give no positive fit. Check **all** compatible null slices first, even if some other coefficient vectors retain positive tight mass.

For $c=m=M$ there are only the following null geometries. In each test require that the candidate support and endpoint density are feasible under the stated holds.

| Design | Null geometry | Side into which loosening must reach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lower estimated, $B>c$ | $e_\theta=c$ | Left |
| Lower estimated, $B=c$ | $(\ell_*,u_*)=(c,c)$ | Left, so $d_\theta<c\le e_\theta$ |
| Upper estimated, $A<c$ | $d_\theta=c$ | Right |
| Upper estimated, $A=c$ | $(\ell_*,u_*)=(c,c)$ | Right, so $d_\theta\le c<e_\theta$ |
| Both estimated | $(\ell_*,u_*)=(c,c)$ | Either side within the support |

For example when $B=c=d_\theta$ a lower cut cannot gain mass at that coefficient vector. A different vector may be feasible because an endpoint is free. The null test examines that vector with its own support. When both cuts are estimated on constants the nominal tight slice is null for every continuous parent. The null test thus decides the complete constant-sample case for that design.

**Proved, positive finite escape heights.** After the null test, the global comparison for the tight window applies pointwise to its positive-mass slices, with the original holds unchanged. For $0<S=\sup L(\theta,W_*)<\infty$, any sequence with joint heights tending to $S$ must have tight heights tending to $S$ and $P_\theta(W_*)/P_\theta(W)\to1$. The conditional law on the looser window is a mixture of the tighter law and the normalized removed part, with removed weight $1-P_\theta(W_*)/P_\theta(W)$. Thus their total variation distance tends to zero. This proves transfer of competitive limiting laws at a finite positive supremum. At an infinite supremum the identity gives no such ratio limit. A divergence witness can settle nonattainment without exhausting divergent paths. At attained height, an excluded face tying the fit does not displace it.

## Applying the fixed-window proofs

All comparisons below are in exact arithmetic. The windows displayed in the regime sections are held fixed **for the realized sample**. In a monotone transformed coordinate, change both the observations and the cuts and reverse the cut order when the transform is decreasing. The Jacobian at the observations cancels in comparisons if the transform is fixed by the holds. If the transform uses a free coefficient, retain its Jacobian or compare conditional likelihood in the original coordinate. A bounded nominal window does not imply a bounded log window, and clipped support ends remain active in every limit.

The scalar tilt test uses the statistic $T$ and carrier written in the linked proof. If the tilt is positive, the empirical mean must be strictly between the zero-tilt mean and the supremum of $T$ on the displayed window. Its derivative is positive variance on every positive-width interval where the statistic varies. The two-shape beta tests use $\log z,\log(1-z)$ and the gamma tests use $\log u,-u$. Their Hessians are negative definite by linear independence modulo constants on the retained interval. Their coercivity comparisons use a positive-length subinterval where the limiting directional exponent exceeds its empirical mean. For distinct observations that mean is strictly below the exponent maximum, including when observations occur at both cuts. Apply the inward tests only on integrable faces permitted by the holds. In a stationary-height comparison evaluate the linked kernels and reachable excluded heights on the displayed window, retaining exact equalities, feasible joins and inside-density sample traces. Pareto and GPD comparisons at threshold contact use the occupied threshold factors, not the positive-excess formula evaluated by dropping those observations. [Exponential-family proof](2026-11-27-trunc-expfam-math-report.md) · [GB2 kernel and comparison proofs](2026-11-27-trunc-gb2-math-report.md#likelihood-formulas-and-comparison-rules) · [Threshold kernel and comparison proofs](2026-11-27-trunc-misc-math-report.md#normalization-and-comparison-lemmas)

For a pure tilt $e^{tz}$ on a transformed interval, the integral is finite on bounded intervals at every finite $t$, on right rays at $t<0$, and on left rays at $t>0$. The $t=0$ law is uniform in $z$ only on a bounded interval. In log coordinates it pulls back to log-uniform, and other slopes pull back to powers. In physical coordinates a nonzero slope is a truncated exponential. Its uniform limit on $[m,M]$ is admissible as an excluded comparison only when the specified path can reach it under the hold. In particular it is an attained conditional law for the GPD uniform submodel and cannot be imposed generically on GB2 or triangular. The grouped kernels in dgamma are integrated over the underlying unit cells, not evaluated at their endpoints. The narrow-window weak limits on null continuous slices are point masses, excluded from these continuous parent models.

The scope labels in the regime sections follow the two independent fixed-window reviews. Where a row states a stationary-height criterion the linked proof supplies its candidate equations and limits. A one-sided failure row states a verified witness or an eligible face; exhaustion does not follow. General cardinality remains open when the known-window analysis cannot rank or isolate the parent winners. The joint maximizing set is nevertheless the exact union over those parent winners of the cut intervals above. ## Grouped-gamma tests

**Proved.** In dgamma the coefficient domain is $k,r>0$. Use $C_j=\int_j^{j+1} y^{k-1}e^{-ry}dy$, $j\ge0$. Every cell has positive mass; the effective integer set is $L,\ldots,U$. The normalizer is the integral on $[L,U+1]$, with infinity unchanged. A singleton has likelihood one at every compatible coefficient vector. Real nominal lower cuts with effective lower cell $m>0$ range over $(m-1,m]$ and if $m=0$ over all cuts $\le0$. For estimated upper cell $M$, real cuts range over $[M,M+1)$. The parent has no last cell.

For free shape and rate on a nonsingleton, constants have the excluded occupied-cell atom. Exactly two occupied adjacent cells have the empirical Bernoulli limit, and attain iff the two cells exhaust the window. The limit follows from a gamma CLT at the shared cell boundary with its mean shifted by order $1/\sqrt{k}$. On two retained cells the rate odds at each fixed shape decrease strictly to zero because the upper cell has greater conditional mean $y$. At rate zero the grouped-power odds diverge as shape grows. Thus all sufficiently large shapes yield a unique matching positive rate, giving a continuum. The optimum height for empirical odds $o$ is the Bernoulli product in the two conditional probabilities $1/(1+o)$ and $o/(1+o)$. If any two occupied cells are separated by one or more whole cells, strict concavity of $\log y-(r/(k-1))y$ implies loss at one occupied cell along $k\to\infty$. A steep decreasing rate also gives loss at the upper occupied cell. Compare finite fits with the integrable grouped shape-zero kernel $y^{-1}e^{-ry}$ if $L>0$, the rate-zero power $y^{k-1}$ if $U<\infty$, and the corner $1/y$ if both conditions hold. Equality at a finite value suffices. This covers data using three or more cells as well.

At held shape use the maximum of the grouped power height ($U<\infty$; zero height on an unbounded ray) and the first-cell atom height ($r\to\infty$). At held rate use the maximum of the grouped inverse-power exponential ($L>0$) or the zero-cell atom ($L=0$) at shape zero, and the last-cell atom at infinite shape ($U<\infty$; zero height with mass escaping on a ray). Apply the scalar root comparison with finite equality. On two cells occupied at both ends, at held shape the empirical odds must be strictly between zero and the grouped-power endpoint odds. At held rate they must exceed the shape-zero endpoint odds (zero if $L=0$), with no finite upper threshold. These bounds follow from strict ordering of the two cells' means of $-y$ and of $\log y$, respectively. A scalar coefficient fitting these two cells is unique. For more than two retained cells a general count of winning roots is open. ## Explicit moving-endpoint submodels

**Proved, GEV at held $\xi=-1$.** The conditional kernel is $e^{tx}$ for $t=1/\sigma>0$, supported below $e=\mu+\sigma$. At fixed $t$, decreasing $e$ to $M$ has no effect on the numerator once the common factor $t e^{-te}$ cancels, and strictly decreases the denominator when the effective upper cut decreases. Nonconstant data therefore optimize at effective upper cut $M$. The strict mean range is $((\ell_*+M)/2,M)$ for finite $\ell_*$, and $(-\infty,M)$ otherwise. At or below the finite lower mean the excluded face is uniform. At the upper equality, either the interval already has zero width or the increasing exponential with rate tending to infinity concentrates at $M$. A constant at $M$ can alternatively put $e=M$ and loosen a lower cut when that cut is estimated. On attainment the rate is unique. The set of $e$ is $\{M\}$ if $u_*>M$, and $[M,\infty)$ if $u_*=M$. For each such $e$, apply the cut plateau rule at that same endpoint. For sample $(1/2,1)$ with $\ell_*=0$ use the mean $3/4$ on $[0,1]$ to obtain continuum many parent winners when $u_*=1$. With both cuts estimated the sample $(0,1,1)$ gives the same strict interior test. The only way a constant can attain an ordinary finite maximum in this submodel would be to reach the upper statistic limit at finite rate and positive width, which strict positivity of the conditional carrier precludes.

**Proved, GPD at held $\xi=-1$ with threshold and scale free.** For $m<M$ every containing interval after clipping has width at least $M-m$. The support $[\mu,\mu+\sigma]=[m,M]$ attains that lower bound. Every winner has
$$
 \max(\ell_*,\mu)=m,\qquad \min(u_*,\mu+\sigma)=M.
$$
For lower-estimated $B>M$ this means $\mu\le m$ and $\mu+\sigma=M$. If $B=M$, any $\mu+\sigma\ge M$ is allowed. For upper-estimated $A<m$ it means $\mu=m$ and $\mu+\sigma\ge M$; if $A=m$, any $\mu\le m$ is allowed. With both cuts estimated any parent support containing the range wins. The conditional law is uniform on $[m,M]$ in all three cases, with likelihood $(M-m)^{-n}$. The nominal cut fibers follow from parent support contact, so a fitted threshold $\mu=m$ or upper end $\mu+\sigma=M$ permits a plateau on the corresponding estimated side. Constants diverge to $\delta_m$ by taking a support interval of length tending to zero on a side allowed by the fixed cut or by loosening an estimated cut into the support at a null slice.

**Proved, selected triangular masks.** At nonconstant data the retained height is rational on an order stratum of the support endpoints, mode, data and finite cuts. Clearing positive denominators gives $Qw=P$ for the sample height $w>0$. Substituting the tight cuts before eliminating the free coefficients gives a semialgebraic height set. A finite included rightmost height gives all tight winners by taking its fiber; absence of such a height identifies an excluded limit or incompatible data. At positive retained width the conditional density is at most twice the inverse width, by integrating a triangle under the concave height kernel. Nonconstant data therefore cannot diverge. A finite excluded law is a normalized one- or two-sided affine kernel from the limiting strata in the reviewed proof, with a separate point trace if a side shrinks at a sample cut. Exact algebraic projection also detects excluded constant-sample heights, which need a width check first. For $a=-1,b=2$ and sample $(0,1)$, choose $B=1$ or $A=0$ if there is a fixed cut. The maximum is $8/9$, achieved at every mode in $[-1,0]\cup[1,2]$. On either plateau the conditional shape is affine. In between, with $D=(c+1)(2-c)>2$, the height is $4D/(9(D-1)^2)<8/9$. The nominal estimated cuts are strict here because the optimum retained interval is strictly inside the parent support. [Triangular algebraic proof](2026-11-27-trunc-misc-math-report.md#triangular)

## Zero observations in exponentiated Weibull and PGW

**Proved.** When zero is observed and the design admits positive mass at the tight or an expanded window, it retains a right neighborhood of zero. In exponentiated Weibull, if shape or exponent is free, one can choose their product below one and obtain infinite inside density with the other sample factors positive. In PGW the same holds if shape is free. If the endpoint power is held strictly above one, every valid window instead has zero likelihood. A lower-estimated sample of all zeros with fixed upper cut zero has no positive-mass expansion because the support starts at zero. Both-estimated constants and upper-estimated all-zero data with a consistent fixed lower bound can expand upward.

If exponent and shape are held at endpoint power one and scale varies, the broad-scale face on finite upper cut is uniform in physical coordinates. The same expansion of the CDF and density that gives the positive-observation power limit includes the endpoint density. On an infinite upper cut the likelihood tends to zero as scale grows. At small scale the occupied-zero density is proportional to inverse scale, while any fixed positive observation has exponentially small density. This proves that every nonconstant zero-containing sample is decided by the scalar scale score against the broad face, and an all-zero sample on a valid fixed positive-width tight window diverges as scale decreases. For a constant on the null tight slice use expansion first.

For PGW with scale and shape held at $S>0$, shape one, the same reasoning applies at exponent infinity. The zero density grows linearly as $\mathrm{exponent}/S$ and each positive density tends to zero faster than any inverse power of exponent by the survival $\exp(1-(1+x/S)^{\mathrm{exponent}})$. The retained mass tends to one when the positive-width interval starts at zero. At exponent zero the normalized broad kernel is proportional to $(S+x)^{-1}$ on the finite window, including at zero, and on an infinite upper cut the likelihood tends to zero. Thus the scalar exponent comparison extends to zero-containing nonconstant samples in this mask. An all-zero sample on a positive-width window diverges at exponent infinity, with weak limit $\delta_0$.

## Regime results

The continuous sections give the effective-window specialization of the reviewed criterion, failure and cardinality. Compatibility includes valid holds and the inside endpoint density. The null and singular tests precede any ordinary positive-width comparison. Each section also gives the true joint bound set when an ordinary fit attains.

### betapr all free truncate:lower-estimated

Tight nominal window $[m,B]$.

The retained interior is $(m,B)$, with positive observations at the cuts included. Compare in $z(x)=x/(S+x)$ with ordered cuts $z(m)$ and $z(B)$ when that transform is fixed by the holds. The fixed-scale beta test uses the images of the cuts in $z$. Zero-shape faces require cutting away the corresponding singular endpoint. Every estimated cut removes positive mass from a strictly looser cut, because the observation at the extreme is strictly inside the positive parent support. Zero is outside the parent domain.

**Criterion · Proved.** Outside the stated constant-divergence cases, a finite score root meets every eligible beta-prime boundary height. Apply this criterion on the specified positive-mass tight-window branch, after the null-slice and singular tests.

**Failure · Proved.** Every constant sample collapses at its common value. Other nonattainment is a winning eligible beta-prime zero-shape, gamma or power limit. This gives the competing tight-window paths on the stated branch.

**Uniqueness · Open.** Isolate and rank the winning parent roots or determine the maximizing components.

**Null and endpoint cases · Proved.** At a null tight window on a constant sample, a permitted positive-mass expansion with positive finite density gives unbounded likelihood and a weak point mass; without such a slice apply the singular and zero-density rules.

**Estimated cuts · Proved.** Every attaining fit has the unique nominal estimated cut or cuts at the sample extremes.

### dgamma free truncate:lower-estimated

Tight nominal window $[m,B]$.

Use $L=m,\ U=\lfloor B\rfloor$, with infinite $B$ leaving $U$ infinite. A constant is always in the first cell, but the window is a singleton only if $U=m$. Adjacent occupied cells exhaust the window iff $U=M=m+1$. The removed parent mass is strictly positive exactly when a change of a nominal cut adds an integer cell at or above zero.

**Criterion · Proved.** Singletons attain. Constants on multisite windows do not attain. Two adjacent occupied cells attain iff they exhaust the retained set. For separated cells a finite fit must meet all eligible grouped faces. Apply the grouped-gamma tests with these cell ends.

**Failure · Proved.** A constant on a multisite window has an excluded occupied-cell atom; two adjacent occupied cells with any extra cell have an excluded empirical Bernoulli. Separated-cell failure is a winning eligible grouped shape-zero, rate-zero or corner face. Apply the grouped-gamma tests with these cell ends.

**Uniqueness · Open.** Determine the full maximizing set on windows with at least three cells, apart from the proved free nonattainment cases. One retained cell is flat and the two-cell odds are controlled.

**Estimated cuts · Proved.** Each estimated real cut has a nontrivial rounding plateau at every attained fit.

**Adjacent cells · Proved.** For free shape and rate, a sample using both adjacent cells of a two-cell retained set has a continuum of parent maximizers matching the empirical odds. Extra retained cells turn this height into an excluded Bernoulli.

### invburr all free truncate:lower-estimated

Tight nominal window $[m,B]$.

The retained interior is $(m,B)$, with positive observations at the cuts included. Compare in $z(x)=1/x$ with ordered cuts $z(B)$ and $z(m)$ when that transform is fixed by the holds. Reciprocation gives Burr at scale $1/S$, held exactly when $S$ is held. Tail and onset exchange, and the Jacobian $1/x^2$ is independent of the coefficients. Every estimated cut removes positive mass from a strictly looser cut, because the observation at the extreme is strictly inside the positive parent support. Zero is outside the parent domain.

**Criterion · Proved.** Outside the stated divergence branches, a feasible score root or specified finite join meets all eligible excluded heights. Apply this criterion on the specified positive-mass tight-window branch, after the null-slice and singular tests.

**Failure · Proved.** Constants allow unbounded modal collapse. For distinct data the competing ends are eligible fixed-power zero-shape, gamma or pure-power limits, a small-power nonpositive log tilt, and a moving lower wall with its approachable full trace in the forward or reflected log coordinate. This gives the competing tight-window paths on the stated branch.

**Uniqueness · Open.** Isolate and rank the winning parent roots or determine the maximizing components.

**Null and endpoint cases · Proved.** At a null tight window on a constant sample, a permitted positive-mass expansion with positive finite density gives unbounded likelihood and a weak point mass; without such a slice apply the singular and zero-density rules.

**Estimated cuts · Proved.** Every attaining fit has the unique nominal estimated cut or cuts at the sample extremes.

### paralogis all free truncate:lower-estimated

Tight nominal window $[m,B]$.

The retained interior is $(m,B)$, with positive observations at the cuts included. Compare in $z(x)=\log x$ with ordered cuts $z(m)$ and $z(B)$ when that transform is fixed by the holds. The GB2 specialization $p=1,q=d=\mathrm{shape}$ changes both these coordinates together. At held scale a constant equal to it has large-shape divergence if the retained log window starts at the log scale, and its height tends to zero if the interval has a left neighborhood. Every estimated cut removes positive mass from a strictly looser cut, because the observation at the extreme is strictly inside the positive parent support. Zero is outside the parent domain.

**Criterion · Proved.** Constants have unbounded likelihood. For nonconstant data, attainment holds iff a finite score root meets every integrable pure power on the retained log window, including zero tilt on bounded log windows. Apply this criterion on the specified positive-mass tight-window branch, after the null-slice and singular tests.

**Failure · Proved.** Constants collapse at their common value. For nonconstant data only integrable pure powers can win at excluded ends, including nonzero tilts at finite power and escaping scale and zero tilt on bounded log windows. This gives the competing tight-window paths on the stated branch.

**Uniqueness · Open.** Isolate and rank the winning parent roots or determine the maximizing components.

**Null and endpoint cases · Proved.** At a null tight window on a constant sample, a permitted positive-mass expansion with positive finite density gives unbounded likelihood and a weak point mass; without such a slice apply the singular and zero-density rules.

**Estimated cuts · Proved.** Every attaining fit has the unique nominal estimated cut or cuts at the sample extremes.

The table covers 184 held masks and 552 regimes. The companion CSV contains 2506 proved rows including scoped cases. An attainment or failure entry can retain the stated hold and sample restrictions. The bound-set rows cover every regime with an attained positive finite fit. [Proof rows](2026-11-28-trunc-est4-math-data/proofs.csv)

## Implementation audit

None of the target family-and-hold combinations has an implemented truncation route in the modifier atlas, for known or estimated cuts. The design lists Poisson, geometric, normal, binomial, held-size negative binomial and finite-window zeta, and none is in the target set. The R dispatch refuses unsupported truncation before resolving NA cuts. The shared binding dispatch likewise rejects these families. For example `mldgamma(c(2,3), truncate=c(NA_real_,NA_real_))` encounters the documented `truncate` refusal, although on the mathematical design both cells attain their empirical Bernoulli with a continuum of parent fits. This is an availability gap documented by the interface. There is no implemented target status to contradict and hence no status-disagreement sample. [Modifier design](../../design/modifiers.md#availability-and-refusals) · [R route check](../../../bindings/r/R/modifiers.R) · [Shared fit dispatch](../../../bindings/common/modifiers.hpp) · [Modifier inventory](../existence-atlas/modifier-atlas.csv)

## What this changes for the fitter

A positive-mass tight-window solve can reuse the compatible fixed-window criterion, conditional on the realized cuts. A moving support must be clipped at the trial coefficients. At an occupied closed endpoint the inside density supplies the sample factor. The plateau condition then recovers the complete estimated-cut fibers from the winning parent vectors. In particular a fixed all-held model can have more than one maximizing nominal cut. Dgamma can report the sample extremes as canonical representatives and record that real-valued cuts remain nonunique.

On constant continuous data, test for expansion at a null tight slice before declaring an empty event. In particular a fixed opposite cut beyond an occupied parent endpoint can leave a positive nominal width but zero mass at the tight cut. When a permitted expansion gives a positive finite density at the observation, report the divergent point-mass limit rather than returning the zero-width fit. Distinguish singular endpoint densities, support incompatibility and certified finite nonattainment. For a positive-width search with an unresolved certificate, the wrapper's successful-search fallback retains the finite candidate with the uncertified flag. Proven divergence or a refuted candidate requires the corresponding stop. [Wrapper failure rule](../../validation/diagnostics.md#wrapper-failure-handling-rule-r6)

## Reproducible checks

The numerical checks use mpmath at 80 decimal digits on the workstation. The dgamma grid uses shapes $1,2,8,32$ and 230 rate bisections on $[0,64]$ for sample $(2,2,3)$, giving empirical likelihood $4/27$. The GPD grid uses $s=10^{-j}$ for $j=4,8,16,24$ and checks the increasing ray and bounded-window likelihoods and the bounded conditional CDF at excess $1/2$. Exact rational arithmetic checks the held triangular and uniform GPD contact identities for $\varepsilon=10^{-j}$ with $j=1,2,4,8$. The analytical results use the formulas above; these finite grids check witnesses and do not grade any row as written. [Check script](2026-11-28-trunc-est4-math-data/check.py) · [Results](2026-11-28-trunc-est4-math-data/checks.json)

## Open

The remaining attainment and cardinality work is listed by mask below. In particular the general GEV moving-end escape envelope is still open beyond the stated fixed-shape faces and tie divergences. Free-shape GPD with a held threshold separated from the minimum needs a uniform comparison of the joint scale and shape ends, including vanishing retention. The reviewed regular EW and PGW scalar comparisons use positive observations; the zero-observation proof extends the specified scale-only and PGW exponent-only scalar cases at unit endpoint power. General positive-data held-root cardinality remains open where indicated. The triangular height test decides attainment and gives the exact maximizing fiber; an explicit analytic classification of which limiting affine traces win at each mask is open. In divergent mixed-endpoint regimes the one-sided rows prove nonattainment or give a concrete path. An exhaustive statement would require rate comparisons for simultaneous endpoint contact, vanishing retention and shape or scale escape.
